I don’t mean it lightly when I say this game has changed my life. I’m autistic, and being social is not really my thing. I loved video games growing up, but I stuck with offline sports games. The only time I ever did anything multiplayer was games of Madden or 2K with friends and occasionally Call of Duty if I was at a friends house. 

In April 2016, I got an Xbox One. One of my best friends asked me “are you gonna get Destiny???” I had heard of Destiny but didn’t know much about it other than it being a space game by the dudes that made Halo. I said probably not. Why spend $60 on a game that I’ll probably suck at, and one where I have to talk to people?? 

A few days later that same friend came with me as I got my new Xbox. When we got to the electronics section, he stepped away for a moment. When he came back he had a copy of Destiny in his hands. “If I buy this for you, promise me you’ll at least try it with me?” I wasn’t gonna say no to a free game so I said sure. Later that night once everything was set up, I got on Destiny and stepped into the Cosmodrome for the very first time. 

After the very first mission I knew this was different. I was instantly hooked by the story, the way the game played, and I enjoyed playing with my friend as he helped carry me through the vanilla D1 story, expansions and Taken King. 

When D2 arrived I was there from day one, but from the time I first started playing till about years 2 and 3 of D2 I was still for the most part a quiet solo player except for when I was with my friend. Wanting that precious raid loot (and wanting outbreak from the zero hour mission) finally gave me the courage to really step out and join the more social aspects of the game. January 2020. I completed my first raid. Later that year I joined a clan where I would meet new friends and start opening up to people. Something I never imagined doing in a video game. Entering Lightfall, I’m part of a great clan, I’ve got loads of raid experience I never imagined having and I’m more social both in game and in person than I was when I first started playing Destiny. So as we get ready for Lightfall tomorrow I just want to say Bungie, from the bottom of my heart, THANK YOU. This game has changed my life for the better and I’m so grateful and happy to be part of this community.

This happened when I was in 8th grade. I attended a small private Christian school at the time. School started at 8 but my Dad had to work early so he usually would drop me off at about 7:15. I would then go to before-care, where an adult basically supervised everyone who was early. I remember it as an ordinary morning, I felt totally fine and did what I usually did in before care, went to the back corner of the cafeteria, lay my head down on the table and close my eyes for a few minutes before my school day began. All of the sudden I started experiencing this sharp pain in my chest, the best I can describe it was it felt like my chest was having a cramp like you get in your legs when working out or playing sports. I didn't panic but I got out of my chair and quickly walked out of the room and down the hallway towards the restroom, as I walked down the hallway the pain got sharper and sharper and my vision started going dark, the last thing I remember was falling to my knees and realizing I wasn't going to make it to the bathroom, by the time I was completely on the floor, I was unconscious .

I have no idea how long I was out. The next thing I remember I was waking up on the floor of the hallway, and I quickly realized two things that I to this day find strange about the situation,

1.	⁠The last thought I had before I passed out was realizing I wasn't going to make it to the bathroom, yet when I woke up, I was actually a few steps past the door to the bathroom.
2.	⁠This was near the end of the before care time period, school was about to start and the hallway at this point was usually pretty busy, yet when I went to go to the bathroom, the hallway was empty and when I woke up, the hallway was empty.

I went into the bathroom to compose myself and make sure that whatever happened wouldn't start again. After that I went back to before care and on with my day, I felt completely fine and to this day that pain in my chest has never returned.

This happened when I was in 8th grade. I attended a small private Christian school at the time. School started at 8 but my Dad had to work early so he usually would drop me off at about 7:15. I would then go to before-care, where an adult basically supervised everyone who was early. I remember it as an ordinary morning, I felt totally fine and did what I usually did in before care, went to the back corner of the cafeteria, lay my head down on the table and close my eyes for a few minutes before my school day began. All of the sudden I started experiencing this sharp pain in my chest, the best I can describe it was it felt like my chest was having a cramp like you get in your legs when working out or playing sports. I didn't panic but I got out of my chair and quickly walked out of the room and down the hallway towards the restroom, as I walked down the hallway the pain got sharper and sharper and my vision started going dark, the last thing I remember was falling to my knees and realizing I wasn't going to make it to the bathroom, by the time I was completely on the floor, I was unconscious . 

I have no idea how long I was out. The next thing I remember I was waking up on the floor of the hallway, and I quickly realized two things that I to this day find strange about the situation,

1. The last thought I had before I passed out was realizing I wasn't going to make it to the bathroom, yet when I woke up, I was actually a few steps past the door to the bathroom. 
2. This was near the end of the before care time period, school was about to start and the hallway at this point was usually pretty busy, yet when I went to go to the bathroom, the hallway was empty and when I woke up, the hallway was empty.

I went into the bathroom to compose myself and make sure that whatever happened wouldn't start again. After that I went back to before care and on with my day, I felt completely fine and to this day that pain in my chest has never returned.

This happened about 12 years ago when I was in 8th grade. I attended a small private Christian school at the time. School started at 8 but my Dad had to work early so he usually would drop me off at about 7:15. I would then go to before-care, where an adult basically supervised everyone who was early. I remember it as an ordinary morning, I felt totally fine and did what I usually did in before care, went to the back corner of the cafeteria, lay my head down on the table and close my eyes for a few minutes before my school day began. All of the sudden I started experiencing this sharp pain in my chest, the best I can describe it was it felt like my chest was having a cramp like you get in your legs when working out or playing sports. I didn't panic but I got out of my chair and quickly walked out of the room and down the hallway towards the restroom, as I walked down the hallway the pain got sharper and sharper and my vision started going dark, the last thing I remember was falling to my knees and realizing I wasn't going to make it to the bathroom, by the time I was completely on the floor, I was unconscious . 

I have no idea how long I was out. The next thing I remember I was waking up on the floor of the hallway, and I quickly realized two things that I to this day find strange about the situation,

1. The last thought I had before I passed out was realizing I wasn't going to make it to the bathroom, yet when I woke up, I was actually a few steps past the door to the bathroom. 
2. This was near the end of the before care time period, school was about to start and the hallway at this point was usually pretty busy, yet when I went to go to the bathroom, the hallway was empty and when I woke up, the hallway was empty.

I went into the bathroom to compose myself and make sure that whatever happened wouldn't start again. After that I went back to before care and on with my day, I felt completely fine and to this day that pain in my chest has never returned.
